title: Getting Good | The Point Magazine
gist: A first-person report from the October 2025 Effective Altruism Global conference in New York argues that EA's capital and talent have pivoted sharply toward AI safety (roughly half the movement's labor and money, 27 of 50 job-fair stalls), away from global health and animal welfare. It contrasts this with EA's low-cost, measurable wins such as lead-paint regulation and shrimp stunning, and it defends the movement against academic critics.

themes.theme: EA capital rotating into AI safety

insights.claim: Insiders estimate that AI safety now consumes about half of the effective altruism movement's labor and capital, a pivot away from its long-standing global health and animal welfare commitments.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: EA philanthropic flows are a large, concentrated funding source for AI alignment and governance orgs; watch for crowding-out of legacy global-health and animal-welfare grantees.
insights.quote: is currently consuming about half of the movement’s labor and capital
insights.locator: The answer is that recently, with the poise

insights.claim: At the EA Global New York job fair, 27 of 50 stalls were devoted to AI research, AI journalism, AI alignment, AI governance or AI solutions.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: The EA talent pipeline is being channeled mostly into AI-related roles, which adds to the supply of mission-driven workers for AI labs and policy shops.
insights.quote: Of fifty stalls, a whopping 27 are devoted to AI research, AI journalism, AI alignment, AI governance, AI solutions
insights.locator: But I am not in luck.

insights.claim: Holden Karnofsky left his post as CEO of the major EA grant maker Coefficient Giving to work full-time on AI safety, and the influential EA job board 80,000 Hours now posts jobs almost exclusively in AI safety.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Senior EA leadership and recruiting infrastructure are now aligned behind AI safety, so this reallocation looks structural rather than cyclical.
insights.locator: Holden Karnofsky, the former CEO

insights.claim: EA Global scheduled four lectures on artificial intelligence, double the number given to either animal welfare or Global Health and Wellbeing. Ajeya Cotra's AI x-risk talk drew the conference's biggest audience.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Attention inside the movement has moved to AI doom scenarios, which supports continued donor demand for alignment research and AI policy advocacy.
insights.locator: And on the stages at EA Global

insights.claim: After two decades of EA influence in Silicon Valley, some of the few billionaires who control frontier AI are effective altruists themselves. EAs see this as a narrow window in which a small group can shape AI's trajectory.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: EA-aligned founders and funders can shape AI lab governance and safety policy, a factor to weigh when assessing AI lab board and regulatory dynamics.
insights.quote: two decades of EA penetration into Silicon Valley means that some of these AI billionaires are already effective altruists themselves
insights.locator: Among effective altruists, however, artificial intelligence

insights.claim: The EA community's catalogue of AI risks includes AI ordering bioweapons from DNA labs, hacking weapons systems to start nuclear war, generating mass misinformation, and deceiving its supervisors.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: These threat models drive the regulatory agenda EA funders push, including DNA synthesis screening, compute controls and misinformation rules.
insights.locator: Among effective altruists, however, artificial intelligence

insights.claim: Eliezer Yudkowsky, called the progenitor of the AI safety field, said in a 2023 TED Talk that his best plan is an international coalition banning large AI training runs, and that he does not expect it to happen.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: The hardline safety position calls for restricting large training runs; any political traction would directly threaten compute-heavy AI business models.
insights.quote: My best bad take is that we need an international coalition banning large AI training runs
insights.locator: “People say to me… ‘What’s your ask?’”

insights.claim: The author argues that the AI safety turn is barely utilitarian because it counts future lives rather than joy and suffering, and that saving the world suits political leaders better than the marginal effective altruist.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Internal skepticism about the AI pivot could eventually rebalance EA funding back toward measurable near-term causes.
insights.quote: this turn toward AI safety is barely even utilitarian, since its concern is not with joy and suffering but with lives
insights.locator: As I leave the conference, jobless and annoyed

insights.claim: Animal-welfare advocates within EA, including undercover farm investigator Ronen Bar, back AI safety because a dominant AI, aligned or not, will affect animals too. This produces an unspoken truce among EA's cause areas rather than open conflict.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Legacy EA constituencies are unlikely to resist the AI reallocation, which reinforces the durability of AI safety funding.
insights.quote: Either way, ignoring AI is not wise, from an animal point of view.
insights.locator: I pose this question to Ronen Bar

insights.claim: Longtermism traces to Nick Bostrom's 2003 paper 'Astronomical Waste' and Toby Ord's 2020 book The Precipice. Both hold that the trillions of future people outweigh present concerns, so preventing existential risks outranks near-term aid.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Expected-value reasoning over near-infinite futures explains why EA money flows to low-probability, high-impact risks such as AI and pandemics instead of proven health interventions.
insights.locator: AI safety falls into the traditional domain

insights.claim: Toby Ord's list of existential risks covers asteroid impact, supervolcanoes, stellar explosions, nuclear war, climate change, other environmental damage, natural and engineered pandemics, and unaligned AI. Unaligned AI is the foremost concern among effective altruists.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: This list maps onto the EA grant priorities (biosecurity, AI governance, nuclear risk) that shape nonprofit and policy funding.
insights.locator: Ord’s proposed list of x-risks

insights.claim: Domestic crime costs the United States at least $300 billion a year in policing, prisons and courts, not counting the social costs of community violence.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Any intervention that measurably cuts crime has a very large implied fiscal payoff.
insights.locator: For a more familiar example, take domestic crime

insights.claim: US violent crime rates since the 1930s track levels of lead in preschoolers' blood taken 23 years earlier, and protecting populations from lead exposure has been shown to cut violent crime by as much as 56 percent.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Lead-abatement policy is a high-return public-health lever; watch regulation affecting paint and pigment makers in emerging markets.
insights.quote: reduce violent crime by as much as 56 percent
insights.locator: Alright, but what if I told you

insights.claim: In 2024, after lobbying by the Lead Exposure Elimination Project and its partners, Nigeria agreed to implement enforceable regulations on the sale of lead paint. EAs have pursued similar lead-free paint mandates with officials in Malawi.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Small EA-funded advocacy teams are driving product regulation in African markets, a reformulation risk and opportunity for paint suppliers there.
insights.locator: So instead of making murals about urban decay

insights.claim: Around 85 billion land animals and trillions of fish are raised and slaughtered each year, yet total annual funding for farmed and wild animal welfare is under $300 million, several times less than what Americans spend on pet Halloween costumes.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Animal welfare remains a tiny, underfunded cause relative to its scale, so marginal grant money can move corporate supply-chain standards.
insights.locator: the yearly budget for both farmed and wild animal welfare

insights.claim: The Shrimp Welfare Project buys industrial electrical stunners from the Norwegian company Optimar at $55,000 per unit and gives them free to shrimp farmers. Each unit can stun over ten metric tons of shrimp per hour, and the project claims 1,400 shrimp stunned per dollar donated.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Philanthropy is subsidizing welfare equipment adoption in aquaculture (Vietnam, India, Ecuador and others), creating demand for stunner makers and 'Humanely Stunned' labeling.
insights.quote: with 1,400 shrimp stunned per dollar donated
insights.locator: But Andrés Jiménez Zorrilla and Aaron Boddy

insights.claim: Fish and crustaceans are the only mass-farmed animals without stunning regulations, which leaves farmed shrimp as a regulatory gap that welfare groups are targeting.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Future stunning rules for seafood are a plausible compliance cost for shrimp and fish producers and exporters.
insights.quote: Fish and crustaceans are the only mass-farmed animals without stunning regulations.
insights.locator: But Andrés Jiménez Zorrilla and Aaron Boddy

insights.claim: Cage-free egg campaigns have freed several billion hens worldwide from cages over the past two decades despite corporate backsliding. Activists are protesting Marriott International over caged-hen eggs under a pledge made nearly a decade ago.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Missed cage-free deadlines expose hospitality and food companies to activist pressure campaigns and reputational risk.
insights.locator: Just a few blocks down the street

insights.claim: Effective altruists prefer 'win-win' welfarist reforms that require no sacrifice from producers over the confrontational tactics of the animal-rights movement, which is split over whether such compromises help or legitimize factory farming.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Expect EA-funded campaigns to push cooperative, industry-friendly standards (stunning, cage-free) rather than bans, which lowers adversarial risk for producers.
insights.locator: They prefer to consider “win-wins,”

insights.claim: Wild animal welfare is an emerging EA cause with only one major organization, the Wild Animal Initiative, whose research remains mostly speculative. Up to a billion birds a year are estimated to die from window collisions in North America.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: This is a nascent, speculative cause area; there is little near-term market relevance beyond bird-safe building materials.
insights.locator: “The literature estimates suggest that up to a billion birds

insights.claim: Giving What We Can, led by CEO Sjir Hoeijmakers, says over eleven thousand people have pledged 10 percent of their income, directing over sixty million dollars a year to charity. Hoeijmakers personally donates 50 percent of his income.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Retail EA giving is modest (about $60M a year) compared with large grant makers, so the movement's direction is set mostly by a few big funders.
insights.quote: I donate 50 percent of my income.
insights.locator: “We encourage people to pledge 10 percent

insights.claim: Evidence Action says $17 can provide ten Kenyan children with clean water for a year, the kind of cost-per-outcome figure that drives EA global-health giving.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: This cost-effectiveness benchmark is now competing for EA dollars against AI safety.
insights.locator: By donating seventeen dollars to a charity

insights.claim: Soylent, founded in 2013 with backing from Y Combinator and Andreessen Horowitz as a futuristic lifehack, is now sold mainly in suburban Walmarts to people with throat cancer and IBS. It is still a staple at EA gatherings.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Soylent is a case study of a VC-backed consumer 'lifehack' that repositioned into a mass-retail medical-nutrition niche.
insights.locator: Soylent was first cooked up in San Francisco

insights.claim: Effective altruism is broadly disliked across the US spectrum, so much that interviewees advised the author to publish under a pseudonym because EA affiliation can hurt employment prospects.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: EA's reputational toxicity (post-scandal) limits its mainstream political coalition-building, which may cap the policy reach of its AI safety agenda.
insights.quote: They are too self-righteous for Silicon Valley and not self-righteous enough for the universities.
insights.locator: Most people I know are scornful of effective altruism

themes.theme: Critics versus EA as a purpose movement

insights.claim: Critics of effective altruism split into two camps. Academics such as Amia Srinivasan and Daron Acemoglu call its ethics shallow, while others such as John Gray and Ari Schulman see it as deforming adherents' lives. Leif Wenar's 'The Deaths of Effective Altruism' is the author's pick for the strongest critique.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: Wenar's critique, that EAs stop listening to experts and local beneficiaries, is the main execution risk for EA-funded development interventions.
insights.quote: save lives by being clever—the philosopher’s way of being the hero
insights.locator: To my mind, the best blow ever landed

insights.claim: The author argues that effective altruism works as a quasi-religion for young elites, offering community, purpose and rituals around diet, vocation and charity, and that critics offer no compelling alternative for a generation said to be in a crisis of purpose.
insights.speaker: Harry Levov
insights.so_what: EA's durable pull on elite graduates keeps a steady supply of talent and donors flowing into its chosen causes, today mainly AI safety.
insights.quote: it must take a very good imagination, or very bad intentions, to ignore effective altruism
insights.locator: For a young, bright college student
